The paper compares dynamical-variable blowups with a separate classification based on an assumed Hubble history.

destinations.title: Can scalar or fluid dark energy reproduce the observed ΛCDM-like expansion through the present while allowing substantially different future evolution, including delayed disruption of bound structures and finite-time singularities?
Can a nonsingular universe with repeatedly similar radiation, matter and scalar-driven expansion phases make the current matter–dark-energy coincidence typical in cosmic time?
Can the observed matter–dark-energy coincidence infer the duration of the current cycle when the cyclic model does not predict that duration?

Matter dilutes as a^-3, whereas dark energy with w near -1 dilutes much more slowly. The coincidence question asks why the current densities are comparable. This paper evaluates whether comparable densities occupy a substantial fraction of cosmic time.
Why observe comparable matter and dark-energy densities if acceleration has an indefinitely long future? The paper investigates whether limiting that future reduces the temporal coincidence.
